## Overview

Reach a GaiaDesk desk from a script, an agent or a terminal.

```text
gaiadesk-cli <command> [options]
```

`gaiadesk-cli <command> --help` (or `gaiadesk-cli help <command>`) for each one.
`gaiadesk-cli --version [--json]` — the release (and, with --json, a feature list to detect).

```text
JSON (every command that takes --json): failures are one envelope on stdout,
  {"error":{"kind":"usage|refused|unreachable|connection_lost|failed|protocol","message":"…"}},
  with the same exit codes as without it. `gaiadesk-cli help json` for the shapes and what changed.
stdout is only ever the result; progress and notes go to stderr, and -q/--quiet silences them on the
  desk operations (cp, run, wait, logs, ps, kill, stats, sync, pull-changed, …). Errors always print.
```

```text
credentials (every command that reaches a desk — the same rule for all of them):
  --code <c> --allow-code-in-argv   the code on the command line (refused without the second flag:
                                    every user on this machine can read a command line)
  --token-file <file>               a scoped agent token (`gaiadesk-cli token create`), chmod 600
  $GAIADESK_TOKEN_FILE              the same, from the environment
  $GAIADESK_CODE                    the desk's code or password
  otherwise an echo-free prompt — only on a terminal; without one the command fails and says so.
The connection is held for later commands (--persist, default 10m), per desk AND credential.
```

```text
--via api (exec, run, ps, logs, wait, kill, cp, stats, token): through the hosted GaiaDesk API
  instead of peer to peer — for a machine that cannot reach the desk directly. End-to-end
  encrypted whenever the desk publishes its key. The same output. Calls as you: `gaiadesk-cli
  login` (not the app's sign-in, which is this computer's own) or $GAIADESK_API_KEY; the desk
  sees your agent token (--token-file) or your own account.
Docs: https://gaiadesk.net/docs/cli-for-agents
```

## alias

Save a short name for a desk id.

**Usage**

```text
gaiadesk-cli alias <name> <desk-id>       set or update an alias
gaiadesk-cli alias rm <name>              remove an alias
gaiadesk-cli alias list                   show all aliases (default when no args)
```

**Subcommands:** `rm`, `list`

Aliases are saved in ~/.gaiadesk/config.toml and work anywhere --desk &lt;id&gt; is accepted:
exec, shell, cp, forward, run, ps, logs, kill, token, audit, stats, measure, and the
desk:&lt;path&gt; notation of cp and forward.

**Examples**

```sh
gaiadesk-cli alias build-box 123456789     # write the alias
gaiadesk-cli exec --desk build-box -- hostname
gaiadesk-cli cp build-box:/var/log/app.log ./log.txt
gaiadesk-cli alias list                    # list all aliases
gaiadesk-cli alias rm build-box            # remove it
```

The config file is ~/.gaiadesk/config.toml (or $GAIADESK_DATA_DIR/config.toml).
Alias names may contain letters, digits, hyphens and underscores.

exit codes: 0 done · 255 could not read or write the config file.

## devices

The desks you can reach.

**Usage**

```text
gaiadesk-cli devices [--json] [--probe] [-d <desk-id>] [--token-file <file>]
```

With no credential flags it uses this machine's sign-in — usually the GaiaDesk app's account —
and says so on stderr ("signed in as &lt;email&gt; (from the GaiaDesk app on this machine)"); --json
adds "identity": {"source": "app|login|token|none", "account": "&lt;email&gt;"|null} (see `whoami`).

Lists, merged by desk id: your account's and your team's desks (from the GaiaDesk server, when
this machine is signed in), desks paired with this machine (LAN), GaiaDesk Mesh peers, and desks
this CLI has connected to before — with hostname, OS, version, owner and last seen.

```text
ONLINE is presence only: the desk's GaiaDesk holds a connection to the server (or the LAN/Mesh
saw it). `online(silent 5m)`: the server has not heard from it for that long — likely a dead
connection. REACH is whether commands actually get through: this machine's last connect to it
(`ok 4 min ago via Mesh`) or last failure and where it stuck (`failed 2 min ago: relay_down`):
  no_route            not found on the LAN or Mesh        relay_down       the server did not answer
  desk_not_answering  asked, never answered: busy, stuck, or waiting for someone to approve
  asleep / restarting the desk is asleep / updating        no_data_channel  accepted, no path carried it
  agent_not_answering connected, but its GaiaDesk did not answer a round trip (probe)
```

**Options**

| Flag | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--probe` | dial each desk NOW (4 at a time, 15s each): route and round-trip time, or the step it failed at; exits 1 if a dialled desk was unreachable. Presents a token only to the desk it names, and a code ($GAIADESK_CODE, --code) only with -d; a desk with no credential is not dialled |
| `-d, --desk-id <id>` | only this desk |
| `--json` | one JSON object: devices[] with online, reachable, last_ok, last_failure, probe, signal_idle_secs, anytime |

> **JSON:** with `--json` this command prints one JSON document on stdout (or the error envelope `{"error":{"kind","message"}}` on failure). The exact shape is defined in the JSON Schema printed by `gaiadesk-cli schema --json`; see also [JSON output](#json-output).

## wake

Ring a sleeping desk's doorbell.

**Usage**

```text
gaiadesk-cli wake <desk> [--wait <seconds>] [--json]
```

Sends a wake signal to a sleeping desk via its doorbell socket or LAN helper.
If the desk already holds a connection to the server it returns immediately.
&lt;desk&gt; is an id or a name (`desk add`, `alias`).

The doorbell is rung by the GaiaDesk server, for the desk's account or team: so `wake` signs in as
an ACCOUNT — $GAIADESK_API_KEY (through the hosted API), `gaiadesk-cli login`, $GAIADESK_TOKEN, or
the GaiaDesk app's sign-in on this machine. A desk's code or an agent token never reaches the
server and cannot ring it.

**Options**

| Flag | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--wait <n>` | wait up to n seconds for the desk to come online (default: 60, at most 90; 0: fire and forget) |
| `--json` | one object {desk_id, online, woke, already_online, rang, waited_ms}; a failure is the envelope {"error":{kind,message,reason}} (`gaiadesk-cli help json`) |

exit codes: 0 online (or already was); 1 rung but not online within --wait, or nothing can wake it
(reason no_wake_path); 254 refused (not signed in, not your desk); 255 this CLI's own error.

> **JSON:** with `--json` this command prints one JSON document on stdout (or the error envelope `{"error":{"kind","message"}}` on failure). The exact shape is defined in the JSON Schema printed by `gaiadesk-cli schema --json`; see also [JSON output](#json-output).

## presence

A desk's online/offline history.

**Usage**

```text
gaiadesk-cli presence <desk> [--since <duration>] [--json]
```

Every transition the GaiaDesk server recorded, oldest first, with the time in UTC and the cause:
online, asleep (the computer slept), offline (shut down, quit, updating, network, or nothing
heard), woke (from sleep) and rebooted. Sleep, reboot and network causes come from the desk's own
word when it reconnects (GaiaDesk 0.10.357 and later); an older desk shows the server's reason.
&lt;desk&gt; is an id or a name (`desk add`, `alias`). Signs in as an ACCOUNT, like `wake`:
$GAIADESK_API_KEY, `gaiadesk-cli login`, $GAIADESK_TOKEN or the app's sign-in on this machine.

**Options**

| Flag | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--since <d>` | how far back: 90m, 24h (default), 7d; the log keeps 30 days |
| `--json` | an array of {at, at_unix, state, cause, cause_text}, oldest first; a failure is the envelope {"error":{kind,message,reason}} |

exit codes: 0 listed (even when empty); 254 refused (not signed in, not your desk); 255 this CLI's
own error.

> **JSON:** with `--json` this command prints one JSON document on stdout (or the error envelope `{"error":{"kind","message"}}` on failure). The exact shape is defined in the JSON Schema printed by `gaiadesk-cli schema --json`; see also [JSON output](#json-output).

## ping

Is a desk reachable, and how fast. No session is left behind.

**Usage**

```text
gaiadesk-cli ping <desk> [--json] [--code <c> --allow-code-in-argv | --token-file <file>]
```

A fresh connect and one round trip (`devices --probe` for one desk). An asleep desk says so and
names `wake`; an offline one says when it was last seen. Exit 0 reachable, 1 not. --json prints the
desk's `devices` row: `state` (online | asleep | offline | unknown), `last_seen`, `free_disk_mb`,
`probe`.

> **JSON:** with `--json` this command prints one JSON document on stdout (or the error envelope `{"error":{"kind","message"}}` on failure). The exact shape is defined in the JSON Schema printed by `gaiadesk-cli schema --json`; see also [JSON output](#json-output).

## status

One look at a desk.

**Usage**

```text
gaiadesk-cli status <desk> [--json] [-q]
```

Its presence from the GaiaDesk server — online, asleep (wakeable: `gaiadesk-cli wake`) or offline,
with when it was last seen — and, ONLY when it is online, a connection for its CPU and load,
memory, free space on each volume, uptime and the background jobs running now (the `stats` and
`ps` figures). An asleep or offline desk is never dialled, so this is fast either way. A desk not
on your account (reached by its code) is dialled. Exit 0 online and answering, 1 not, 255 this
CLI's own error. --json: {desk, state, online, dialled, name, os, last_seen, stats, jobs, error}.

```text
credentials (see `gaiadesk-cli --help` for the order):
  --token-file <file>      a scoped agent token (or $GAIADESK_TOKEN_FILE)
  --code <code>            the desk's code — refused unless --allow-code-in-argv too (prefer
                           $GAIADESK_CODE or the prompt: argv is visible to other users)
  --connect-timeout <dur>  give up reaching the desk after <dur> (default 60s; 30s, 3m)
```

> **JSON:** with `--json` this command prints one JSON document on stdout (or the error envelope `{"error":{"kind","message"}}` on failure). The exact shape is defined in the JSON Schema printed by `gaiadesk-cli schema --json`; see also [JSON output](#json-output).

## desk

Name a desk and keep its access code.

**Usage**

```text
gaiadesk-cli desk add <name> <desk-id> [--code-file <file> | --code-stdin]
gaiadesk-cli desk rm <name>
gaiadesk-cli desk list [--json]
```

**Subcommands:** `add`, `rm`, `list`

`desk add charlie 123456789` makes `charlie` an alias for the id (the same one `alias` writes) and
stores the desk's access code, so every command can name the desk — `--desk-id charlie`,
`cp ./a charlie:work/`, `sync ./src charlie:app` — with no $GAIADESK_CODE. Without a code flag it
asks on the terminal (no echo).
The code is kept in a private file (~/.gaiadesk/desk-codes/&lt;id&gt;, readable by you alone), not the OS
keychain: the CLI runs over SSH and in CI, where a keychain is locked or absent.
A code flag, $GAIADESK_CODE or a token still wins over the stored one.
A legacy ~/.config/gaiadesk/desks file (`name id [code-file]` per line) is read as well.

> **JSON:** with `--json` this command prints one JSON document on stdout (or the error envelope `{"error":{"kind","message"}}` on failure). The exact shape is defined in the JSON Schema printed by `gaiadesk-cli schema --json`; see also [JSON output](#json-output).

## sync

Mirror a local folder onto a desk, sending only what changed.

**Usage**

```text
gaiadesk-cli sync [--delete] [--exclude <glob>]… [--gitignore] [--keep-newer | --force]
                  [--compress auto|on|off] [--retries N] [--full] [--allow-secrets] [--dry-run]
                  [--json] [--min-free <MB> | --no-free-check] <localdir> <desk>:<path>
```

```text
The folder's CONTENTS land in <path> on the desk (its parent must exist). Every file travels as `cp`
does: written as `<name>.gdpart`, SHA-256 checked, renamed into place — never half a file under the
real name — and the upload is refused up front if it would leave the desk's disk under the floor.
What counts as changed: this machine records each file's size and time as last sent, per desk and
destination; a new file or a different size or time is sent. --full sends everything again.
Desk edits are not overwritten: the record also keeps each file's size and time on the desk, and a
desk file about to be replaced or removed that differs from it (or that sync never sent) stops the
sync — "3 file(s) on the desk changed since your last sync: …" (exit 1). The first sync to a
destination has no record: a desk file there newer than the local one stops it — "2 file(s) on the
desk are newer than yours — rerun with --keep-newer to skip them or --force to overwrite" (exit 1,
--json reason newer_on_desk; later: changed_on_desk); the others are replaced as `cp` does.
--force       replace (or remove) them anyway.
--keep-newer  never replace a desk file newer than the local one (left as it is, and named).
.gaiadeskignore in <localdir> lists what never goes (gitignore syntax: *, **, ?, [a-z], !, a
trailing / for folders, a leading / for this folder only) — e.g. per-OS build pointer files.
--gitignore   also honour every .gitignore under <localdir>, and skip .git/.
--compress    as `cp --compress` (default auto).
--retries <n> as `cp --retries`: a lost desk or connection is tried again up to <n> times, 2s, 4s,
              8s… apart, each try resuming the files cut off (default 3 once a file over 100 MB
              is sent, else 0).
--delete  also removes from the desk the files an earlier sync sent that are gone here. It never
          touches a file `sync` did not put there; without --delete nothing is removed.
--exclude a name or path glob (* and ?); a folder that matches is skipped. Repeatable.
--allow-secrets  send `.env`, `*.pem`, `*.key`, ssh keys (left home by default).
--dry-run  say what would be sent and removed.
Symlinks are skipped.
```

usage: gaiadesk-cli sync --git &lt;localrepo&gt; --ref &lt;rev&gt; --to &lt;desk&gt;:&lt;dir&gt; [--keep &lt;dir&gt;]… [--json]

A commit, not a folder: `git bundle`s &lt;rev&gt; of the local repository (only the commits the desk
lacks when its checkout is at one this repository has), copies the bundle, and on the desk makes
&lt;dir&gt; a checkout of exactly that commit — git init (or fetch into the one there), checkout
--detach, `git clean -fdx`. Untracked and ignored files on the desk go, EXCEPT `target/` and each
--keep &lt;dir&gt; (repeatable), so build caches survive. Changes made on the desk are discarded: pull
them first (`pull-changed`). A &lt;dir&gt; that holds files and is not a git checkout is refused, never
wiped. Needs git here and on the desk (a clear error when the desk has none); Windows, macOS and
Linux desks. Prints the commit (--json: commit, previous, bundle_bytes, incremental).

```text
output:
  -q, --quiet              no progress or notes on stderr (the result and errors still print)
```

```text
credentials (see `gaiadesk-cli --help` for the order):
  --token-file <file>      a scoped agent token (or $GAIADESK_TOKEN_FILE)
  --code <code>            the desk's code — refused unless --allow-code-in-argv too (prefer
                           $GAIADESK_CODE or the prompt: argv is visible to other users)
  --connect-timeout <dur>  give up reaching the desk after <dur> (default 60s; 30s, 3m)
```

> **JSON:** with `--json` this command prints one JSON document on stdout (or the error envelope `{"error":{"kind","message"}}` on failure). The exact shape is defined in the JSON Schema printed by `gaiadesk-cli schema --json`; see also [JSON output](#json-output).

## pull-changed

Copy a desk checkout's changes back here.

**Usage**

```text
gaiadesk-cli pull-changed <desk>:<dir> [--to <localdir>] [--delete] [--retries N] [--json]
```

Runs `git status --porcelain` in &lt;dir&gt; on the desk and copies every modified, added, renamed and
untracked file into the same place under &lt;localdir&gt; (default: the current directory) — what an
agent or a build changed after `sync --git`. Deleted files are left here and named on stderr;
--delete removes them too. Prints one line per file (`pulled <path>`, `deleted <path>`); --json:
{desk, source, destination, files:[{path, status, action}], failed}. Exit 0, or 1 when a file
failed. Needs git on the desk. --retries &lt;n&gt;: as `cp --retries` (default 0) — a lost desk or
connection pulls again up to &lt;n&gt; times, 2s, 4s, 8s… apart, a file cut off resuming where it stopped.

```text
output:
  -q, --quiet              no progress or notes on stderr (the result and errors still print)
```

```text
credentials (see `gaiadesk-cli --help` for the order):
  --token-file <file>      a scoped agent token (or $GAIADESK_TOKEN_FILE)
  --code <code>            the desk's code — refused unless --allow-code-in-argv too (prefer
                           $GAIADESK_CODE or the prompt: argv is visible to other users)
  --connect-timeout <dur>  give up reaching the desk after <dur> (default 60s; 30s, 3m)
```

> **JSON:** with `--json` this command prints one JSON document on stdout (or the error envelope `{"error":{"kind","message"}}` on failure). The exact shape is defined in the JSON Schema printed by `gaiadesk-cli schema --json`; see also [JSON output](#json-output).

## tool

A per-user toolchain on a desk, no admin needed.

**Usage**

```text
gaiadesk-cli tool <name>@<version> --desk-id <desk> [--json]
gaiadesk-cli run --detach --name <job> --desk-id <desk> --tool go@1.26 -- go test ./...
```

Tools: go, node. The version is a release or its prefix (`go@1.26` is the newest 1.26.x). The desk
downloads the vendor's official archive, checks the published SHA-256, unpacks beside the final
folder and renames it into place (so a failed unpack is never taken for an install), under
%LOCALAPPDATA%\GaiaDesk\tools (Windows) or ~/.cache/gaiadesk/tools. Prints the bin directory.
Already installed: nothing is downloaded. `run --tool <name>@<version>` (repeatable) installs it and
puts it first on the job's PATH. The desk needs internet access to go.dev / nodejs.org.

```text
output:
  -q, --quiet              no progress or notes on stderr (the result and errors still print)
```

```text
credentials (see `gaiadesk-cli --help` for the order):
  --token-file <file>      a scoped agent token (or $GAIADESK_TOKEN_FILE)
  --code <code>            the desk's code — refused unless --allow-code-in-argv too (prefer
                           $GAIADESK_CODE or the prompt: argv is visible to other users)
  --connect-timeout <dur>  give up reaching the desk after <dur> (default 60s; 30s, 3m)
```

> **JSON:** with `--json` this command prints one JSON document on stdout (or the error envelope `{"error":{"kind","message"}}` on failure). The exact shape is defined in the JSON Schema printed by `gaiadesk-cli schema --json`; see also [JSON output](#json-output).

## whoami

Who this CLI is signed in as.

**Usage**

```text
gaiadesk-cli whoami [--json]
```

```text
The GaiaDesk account the CLI presents to the server (to list your desks, to reach them through
it), and where that sign-in comes from:
  app     the GaiaDesk app on this machine is signed in, and the CLI uses its account
  login   `gaiadesk-cli login`
  token   $GAIADESK_TOKEN (or an SDK's account_token)
  none    nobody: only desks on the LAN, on Mesh, or reached with a code or token
--json: {"source":"app|login|token|none","account":"<email>"|null}. Exit 0 signed in, 1 not.
```

> **JSON:** with `--json` this command prints one JSON document on stdout (or the error envelope `{"error":{"kind","message"}}` on failure). The exact shape is defined in the JSON Schema printed by `gaiadesk-cli schema --json`; see also [JSON output](#json-output).

## exec

Run ONE command on a desk and exit with its exit code.

**Usage**

```text
gaiadesk-cli exec --desk-id <id> [options] -- <command> [args...]
```

Like `ssh host cmd`: the command's stdout goes to stdout and its stderr to stderr, unaltered (no
echo, no prompt, no escape codes, no console width — plain pipes, on Windows too); stdin is closed
unless -i; the exit code is the command's own. With an agent token, the token needs the `exec`
scope; without it the desk refuses the command (exit 254, with the desk's reason).

```text
LONG RUNS — `exec` belongs to its connection: if the link drops you lose its output and its exit
  code, and there is no re-attaching to it (the command itself keeps running on the desk, unless
  --kill-tree-on-disconnect, or an older GaiaDesk, ends its whole process tree). Anything long
  (builds, test suites, renders) goes through
      gaiadesk-cli run --detach --name <job> … -- <cmd>      (the desk owns the job)
      gaiadesk-cli wait <job> --desk-id <id> [--timeout <dur>]   (reconnects by itself; exit 124
                                                              timed out, 75 link lost, else the job's code)
      gaiadesk-cli logs <job> --desk-id <id> [-f]
  so a network blip never costs the run. `exec` is for commands you wait on for minutes at most.
```

```text
WHICH SHELL — the default is the desk's own shell, and it differs by desk:
  macOS/Linux  `$SHELL -l -c '<line>'` — the desk user's LOGIN shell (zsh on a Mac): their PATH and
               profile, and zsh syntax. For portable POSIX scripts, say so: --shell sh (/bin/sh -c).
  Windows      cmd.exe (/d /v:off /s /c), switched to UTF-8 (chcp 65001) first. --shell pwsh for
               PowerShell (pwsh, else Windows PowerShell), with UTF-8 output.
  `--json` and `--verbose` print the shell the desk actually used.
```

**Options**

| Flag | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--desk-id <id>` | the desk (-d) |
| `--shell <s>` | default \| sh \| bash \| zsh \| pwsh (or powershell) \| cmd \| none (see above; pwsh starts with -NoLogo -NoProfile -NonInteractive and a decoded -Command: no prompt, no CLIXML progress on stderr) ONE argument after `--` is a command line for that shell, verbatim (`-- 'ls \| wc -l'`); SEVERAL are separate arguments, each quoted for that shell so the program receives exactly them. `none` runs the program directly with that argument vector. |
| `-n, --no-stdin` | stdin is closed (the default) |
| `-i, --stdin` | forward this terminal's stdin to the command |
| `--timeout <dur>` | stop the command after &lt;dur&gt; (30s, 10m, 2h; 0 = never; default 30m) |
| `--connect-timeout <dur>` | give up reaching the desk after &lt;dur&gt; (default 60s); the error names the step that did not finish (route, server, LAN, the desk's answer) |
| `--cwd <dir>` | start the command in &lt;dir&gt; on the desk (relative: from the desk user's home). A token confined to a directory may only name one inside it — anything else is refused (254); a directory that is not there fails (1) |
| `--workspace <name>` | start the command in `~/.gaiadesk/workspaces/<name>` on the desk, creating the directory if it does not exist. Sets --cwd when --cwd is absent; an explicit --cwd wins. Also sets GAIADESK_WORKSPACE=&lt;name&gt; in the command's environment. Two agents on the same desk use different names to avoid clobbering each other's files. |
| `--script <file>` | upload a local script to a temp path on the desk and run it — as `run --script` does: the interpreter by extension and the desk's OS (.ps1 powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File, .sh sh, .py python/python3, .cmd/.bat cmd /c; no extension on Unix: sh), so no --shell. Bypasses the 4 KB command-line limit and quoting; words after `--` are its arguments. The temp file (/tmp, C:\Windows\Temp) is removed when it ends. |
| `-e, --env KEY=VALUE` | set an environment variable for the command (repeatable; a later one wins). Values go to the desk in the request and are never logged. |
| `-e, --env KEY` | the same, with the value of $KEY here — keeps a secret off this command line (which other users of this machine can read) |
| `-e, --env KEY=@file` | the value read from a LOCAL file (one trailing newline dropped): sent in memory, never written to the desk's disk (KEY=@@x: the literal @x) |
| `--env-file <file>` | KEY=VALUE lines (# comments, blank lines and `export ` allowed) |
| `--json` | print one JSON object: {exit, remote_code, stdout, stderr, duration_ms, desk, route, mode, shell, timed_out, error, notes, truncated}. `error` is null, or {kind, message[, reason]} (`gaiadesk-cli help json`). A program Windows Smart App Control / WDAC refused to start has reason "blocked_by_os_policy" (and the message says where it is logged) |
| `--json-stream` | one JSON object per line AS IT RUNS: {"event":"stdout","data":…}, {"event":"stderr","data":…}, then {"event":"exit",…} (--json's object without the output) or {"event":"error","exit":N,"error":{…}} |
| `-v, --verbose` | say on stderr how it ran: route, mode (pipes), shell, exit, time |
| `--admin` | run it as ADMINISTRATOR (root on macOS/Linux, SYSTEM on Windows), in the desk's privileged GaiaDesk process. Needs a token with the `admin` scope and the desk owner's Admin access, turned on AT the desk; by default the person at the desk is asked each time (no answer = no). Refused (254) with reason admin_scope_missing \| admin_not_enabled \| admin_denied \| admin_unavailable. Windows Smart App Control still applies to SYSTEM |
| `--raw-args` | send the words after `--` exactly as received (from Git Bash, words it rewrote into `C:/Program Files/Git/…` are otherwise put back, or refused with the fix — see `run --help`) |
| `--kill-tree-on-disconnect` | kill the process and everything it started (its process group on Unix, its Job object on Windows) when THIS CLI disconnects — network drop, Ctrl-C, --timeout, etc. Without this flag the process keeps running on the desk after the CLI exits (background, like an ssh command that outlives its session). With it, a disconnect is a kill. |
| `--persist <dur>` | keep the connection open for later commands for &lt;dur&gt; idle (default 10m, or $GAIADESK_PERSIST; 0 = connect fresh every time) |
| `-q, --quiet` | no progress lines on stderr |

**Examples**

```sh
gaiadesk-cli exec -d 123456789 --shell sh -- 'uname -a; df -h /'
gaiadesk-cli exec -d 123456789 -- hostname   # a Windows desk: cmd.exe
gaiadesk-cli exec -d 123456789 --shell pwsh -- 'Get-Service | Where-Object Status -eq Running'
gaiadesk-cli exec -d 123456789 --cwd /srv/app --json-stream -- 'make test'
gaiadesk-cli exec -d 123456789 --script ./gate.ps1 --shell pwsh -- arg1 arg2
gaiadesk-cli exec -d 123456789 --script ./deploy.sh -e AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
```

```text
credentials (see `gaiadesk-cli --help` for the order):
  --token-file <file>      a scoped agent token (or $GAIADESK_TOKEN_FILE)
  --code <code>            the desk's code — refused unless --allow-code-in-argv too (prefer
                           $GAIADESK_CODE or the prompt: argv is visible to other users)
```

```text
through the hosted API:
  --via api                through the GaiaDesk API instead of peer to peer (end-to-end encrypted
                           when the desk publishes its key); `--via direct` is the default
```

```text
exit codes:
  0-255  the command's own exit code
  124    --timeout ran out (the command was stopped)
  130    interrupted (Ctrl-C)
  75     (`wait` only) the link to the desk was lost and not regained; the job may still be running
  76/77  (`wait` only) the same, and the server says the desk is asleep (76) / offline (77)
  254    the desk refused (wrong code, a token without the scope, no permission, declined)
  255    gaiadesk-cli's own error (offline, unreachable, bad arguments)
```

> **JSON:** with `--json` this command prints one JSON document on stdout (or the error envelope `{"error":{"kind","message"}}` on failure). The exact shape is defined in the JSON Schema printed by `gaiadesk-cli schema --json`; see also [JSON output](#json-output).

## shell

A terminal on a desk, like `ssh host`.

**Usage**

```text
gaiadesk-cli shell --desk-id <id> [options]                  (interactive)
gaiadesk-cli shell --desk-id <id> [options] -- <command>     (one command, like exec)
<script> | gaiadesk-cli shell --desk-id <id> [options]       (a script on stdin)
```

On a terminal, an interactive shell (the desk's own: your login shell on macOS/Linux, cmd.exe on
Windows) at your terminal's size. Not on a terminal — a command after `--`, or a script piped in
— it runs over plain pipes like `exec`: stdout and stderr apart, no prompt, no echo, no console
width, and the exit code is the remote command's (a script's: its last command's). --shell sh
runs a script with /bin/sh instead of the desk user's login shell (zsh on a Mac).

**Options**

| Flag | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--desk-id <id>` | the desk (-d) |
| `--shell <s>` | non-interactive: default \| sh \| pwsh \| cmd (see `exec --help`) |
| `--timeout <dur>` | non-interactive: stop it after &lt;dur&gt; (default 30m; 0 = never) |
| `--json` | non-interactive: one JSON object, as `exec --json` |
| `--cwd <dir>` | start the shell (or the command, or the script) in &lt;dir&gt; on the desk, as `exec --cwd`: inside a confined token's directory or refused (254) |
| `--workspace <name>` | start the shell in `~/.gaiadesk/workspaces/<name>` on the desk, creating it if it does not exist; sets --cwd when --cwd is absent |
| `--admin` | an ADMINISTRATOR shell (root / SYSTEM) — as `exec --admin`: a token with the `admin` scope, the desk owner's Admin access, and (by default) a yes from the person at the desk |
| `--persist <dur>` | share a held connection (see `exec --help`; default 10m) |
| `--connect-timeout <dur>` | give up reaching the desk after &lt;dur&gt; (default 60s) |
| `-v, --verbose` | say on stderr how it ran (non-interactive) |
| `-q, --quiet` | no progress lines |

```text
exit codes (never 0 unless the remote shell or command said 0; the reason is always on stderr):
  0-255  the remote shell's / command's own exit code
  124    --timeout ran out          130  interrupted (Ctrl-C)
  253    remote error: the connection was lost mid-session, or the desk ended the terminal
  254    refused: wrong code, a token without the `exec` scope, no control, declined
  255    could not connect: offline, unreachable, timed out (bad arguments too)
An agent token needs the `exec` scope.
```

```text
credentials (see `gaiadesk-cli --help` for the order):
  --token-file <file>      a scoped agent token (or $GAIADESK_TOKEN_FILE)
  --code <code>            the desk's code — refused unless --allow-code-in-argv too (prefer
                           $GAIADESK_CODE or the prompt: argv is visible to other users)
```

> **JSON:** with `--json` this command prints one JSON document on stdout (or the error envelope `{"error":{"kind","message"}}` on failure). The exact shape is defined in the JSON Schema printed by `gaiadesk-cli schema --json`; see also [JSON output](#json-output).

## cp

Copy files or folders to or from a desk, like `scp`.

**Usage**

```text
gaiadesk-cli cp [-r] [--json] [-v] [--retries N] [--compress M] <local> <desk-id>:<path>   (upload)
gaiadesk-cli cp [-r] [--json] [-v] [--retries N] [--compress M] <desk-id>:<path> <local>   (download)
gaiadesk-cli cp --admin [--json] <local> <desk-id>:</abs/path>   (one file, as administrator)
```

Resumable, uploads AND downloads: an interrupted file is kept as &lt;name&gt;.gdpart, and the same
copy run again continues from its end — after the sender proves, by the SHA-256 of those bytes,
that the part is its own file's beginning. A part that is not (the file changed, or the part is
another file's) is said so and the file is sent whole; nothing is ever spliced. Every file is
checked end to end (SHA-256) before it takes its name. A remote path is relative to the desk
user's home; a trailing / means "into that folder". A token needs the `cp` scope.

**Options**

| Flag | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `-r, --recursive` | copy a folder |
| `--json` | one JSON summary of what moved — and nothing else: no progress or summary line on stderr (add -v for them) |
| `-v, --verbose` | with --json, the progress lines on stderr too |
| `--retries <n>` | when the desk cannot be reached or the connection drops, try again up to &lt;n&gt; times, 2s, 4s, 8s… apart, each try RESUMING (default: 3 once a file over 100 MB is involved, else 0). A refusal or a failed file is final |
| `--min-free <MB>` | refuse an upload that would leave the desk's disk under this (default: scaled to the upload — it must leave its own size free, at least 256 MB, at most the larger of 1 GB and 5% of the volume; under 10 MB it only has to fit). The desk reports its free space first |
| `--no-free-check` | no free-space check (same as --min-free 0) |
| `--admin` | read or write ONE file as administrator (root / SYSTEM) through `exec --admin` — the same token scope, switch and question at the desk; the desk path absolute, no -r, no resume |

Windows paths are shown without the \\?\ prefix.

```text
speed:
  --compress auto|on|off   deflate chunks on the wire (default auto: tried on each file's first MB
                           and kept only if it saves a tenth; zip, gz, xz, 7z, jpg, png, mp4… go as
                           they are). Only between this CLI and a desk that takes it — an older
                           desk gets plain chunks. The file's SHA-256 check is of its own bytes.
                           A download asks the desk for deflated chunks unless off (it then
                           decides as auto). Text, sources and many binaries move 2-5x faster
                           over a slow link; already-compressed files gain nothing
  On a terminal, a live line shows the file, how much of it, the throughput and the ETA (not under
  --json or -q).
```

```text
output:
  -q, --quiet              no progress or notes on stderr (the result and errors still print)
```

```text
credentials (see `gaiadesk-cli --help` for the order):
  --token-file <file>      a scoped agent token (or $GAIADESK_TOKEN_FILE)
  --code <code>            the desk's code — refused unless --allow-code-in-argv too (prefer
                           $GAIADESK_CODE or the prompt: argv is visible to other users)
  --connect-timeout <dur>  give up reaching the desk after <dur> (default 60s; 30s, 3m)
```

```text
through the hosted API:
  --via api                through the GaiaDesk API instead of peer to peer (end-to-end encrypted
                           when the desk publishes its key); `--via direct` is the default
```

exit codes: 0 done; 1 it ran and did not succeed (a file failed, no such job);
254 the desk refused (credential, a token without the scope, permission); 255 this CLI's own error.
The session is the held one `exec` and `shell` use (per desk and credential; $GAIADESK_PERSIST).

> **JSON:** with `--json` this command prints one JSON document on stdout (or the error envelope `{"error":{"kind","message"}}` on failure). The exact shape is defined in the JSON Schema printed by `gaiadesk-cli schema --json`; see also [JSON output](#json-output).

## run

Start a named background job on a desk.

**Usage**

```text
gaiadesk-cli run --detach --name <job> --desk-id <id> [options] -- <command…>
gaiadesk-cli run --wait   --name <job> --desk-id <id> [--collect <glob>]… [options] -- <command…>
```

--detach returns at once (the job runs on); --wait stays until the job ends and exits with ITS
exit code, exactly as `run --detach` then `wait` (the same exit codes as `wait`).

ONE argument after `--` is the command line itself, given to the desk's shell verbatim (cmd.exe on
Windows, sh on macOS/Linux): `-- 'msbuild app.sln /m'`, `-- 'make -j8 && make install'`. Several
arguments are separate words, each quoted for THAT desk's shell; on Windows an argument holding a
cmd metacharacter (&amp; | &lt; &gt; ^ % ! ( ) ") is refused — give the whole line as one argument instead.

THE way to run long work on a desk (builds, tests, renders, backups): the job belongs to the desk's
GaiaDesk host, not to this connection — it keeps running when this command, the connection, or
the terminal you ran it from ends, and when GaiaDesk itself restarts. Read it with `logs` (-f to
follow), list it with `ps`, stop it (and everything it started) with `kill`. On Windows it runs in
a Job object of its own, out of the session's; on macOS/Linux in a session of its own (setsid).
Do not background work inside `exec` (`start /b`, `nohup … &`): exec ends its whole process tree.
For a command whose output you wait for, use `exec`. Needs control of the desk; a token needs the
`jobs` scope.

**Options**

| Flag | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--cwd <dir>` | the directory the job starts in on the desk (inside a confined token's directory, or refused) |
| `--workspace <name>` | start the job in `~/.gaiadesk/workspaces/<name>` on the desk, creating it if it does not exist; sets --cwd when --cwd is absent; injects GAIADESK_WORKSPACE=&lt;name&gt; into the job's environment |
| `-w, --wait` | stay until the job ends; exit with its code (see `wait --help`) |
| `--collect <glob>` | after the job ends, copy the matching files from the job's directory (--workspace / --cwd) back here, at the same relative paths (repeatable; `out/*.zip`, `target/release/app.exe`, a folder; `*` also crosses folders). Implies --wait. A pattern that matches nothing makes a successful job exit 1; --json adds `collected` and `collect_failed` |
| `--collect-to <dir>` | where collected files land (default: `./<name>-artifacts/`) |
| `--shell <s>` | sh \| bash \| zsh \| cmd \| pwsh (or powershell): the shell that runs the command (default: sh -c on macOS/Linux, cmd /c on Windows) |
| `--script <file>` | upload a local script to a temp path on the desk and run THAT as the job (interpreter by extension: .ps1 powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File, .sh sh, .py python, .cmd/.bat cmd /c); words after `--` are its arguments; the temp file is removed when it ends. Pair with --env for values, which need no shell quoting |
| `--tool <name>@<version>` | install (once, no admin) and put go/node first on the job's PATH (repeatable; see `gaiadesk-cli tool --help`) |
| `-e, --env KEY[=VALUE]` | an environment variable for the job (repeatable; a bare KEY takes $KEY here); never logged. KEY=@file reads the value from a LOCAL file (a secret: sent in memory, never written to the desk's disk) |
| `--env-file <file>` | KEY=VALUE lines, as `exec --env-file` |
| `--secret-file NAME=<file>` | a LOCAL file the job needs as a file (a signing key, a kubeconfig): written on the desk for this job only (mode 0600 in a private 0700 folder), its path in $NAME, and overwritten and removed when the job ends — exit, failure, kill, or (if GaiaDesk was not running then) at its next start. Repeatable, 1 MB each; never logged |
| `--raw-args` | send the words after `--` exactly as received (see Git Bash below) |
| `--priority low\|normal\|high` | CPU priority (alias --nice). Windows: the job's priority class; macOS/Linux: nice 10 for low (+ background QoS on a Mac), -5 for high (high needs a GaiaDesk host running as root) |
| `--cpu <percent>` | at most this share of the WHOLE machine, 1-100 (Windows: Job object hard cap; Linux: cgroup v2 CPUQuota; macOS, or Linux without cgroups: GaiaDesk pauses the job to hold it there) |
| `--mem <MB>` | at most this much memory for the job and everything it starts (512, 2G). Windows: Job object limit (allocations past it fail); Linux: cgroup v2 MemoryMax, else RLIMIT_AS + GaiaDesk's watchdog; macOS: GaiaDesk stops the job past it — `ps` shows `killed (memory limit …)` |
| `--keep-awake` | RECOMMENDED for long jobs: the desk does not idle-sleep while the job runs (released when it ends). Off unless asked (the owner's rule); without it a desk that sleeps mid-job leaves `wait` exit 76 (desk_slept). --no-keep-awake overrides a desk whose default is on |
| `--max-runtime <dur>` | stop the job and everything it started after it has run &lt;dur&gt; (30s, 90m, 2h): it ends `killed (max runtime exceeded)` |
| `--json` | the job as JSON (with `limits` and how the desk enforces them); a failure is the envelope (`gaiadesk-cli help json`) |

A job a program in it was refused by Windows Smart App Control / WDAC ends as
`exited (blocked by Windows Smart App Control / WDAC)` with reason "blocked_by_os_policy".
Wait for one to end with `gaiadesk-cli wait <job>` (or start it with --wait).

From Git Bash on Windows: Git Bash rewrites words that look like POSIX paths before this CLI
sees them (`/Users/x/b.sh` arrives as `C:/Program Files/Git/Users/x/b.sh`). For a macOS or
Linux desk, such a word is put back (with a note), and one that cannot be put back for certain
(`/bin/…` and `/usr/bin/…` both become `…/Git/usr/bin/…`) is refused with the fix: run with
MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1. A job that exits 127 within seconds says `command not found: <program>`.

Automation: give a job's runner a scoped, expiring agent token (`gaiadesk-cli token create
--scope jobs,cp --expires 1d --out t.json`, then GAIADESK_TOKEN_FILE=t.json), not $GAIADESK_CODE —
the desk's code opens everything and never expires; a token can be revoked, and its jobs stop.

A desk runs a limited number of jobs at once (16; `ps --json` shows it as `max_running`). A start
past it is not refused: the job waits in state `queued` (with `queue_position`) and starts, in
order, as running jobs end. `kill` takes a queued job out of the line. A host restart drops
the queue (the jobs show as `lost`).

**Examples**

```sh
gaiadesk-cli run -d --name build --desk-id 234567890 --priority low --cpu 50 -- 'msbuild app.sln /m'
gaiadesk-cli run -d --name nightly --desk-id 123456789 --keep-awake --mem 4G -- ./nightly.sh
gaiadesk-cli run --wait --keep-awake --name rel --desk-id ci --workspace rel --collect 'dist/*.zip' -- 'make dist'
```

```text
output:
  -q, --quiet              no progress or notes on stderr (the result and errors still print)
```

```text
credentials (see `gaiadesk-cli --help` for the order):
  --token-file <file>      a scoped agent token (or $GAIADESK_TOKEN_FILE)
  --code <code>            the desk's code — refused unless --allow-code-in-argv too (prefer
                           $GAIADESK_CODE or the prompt: argv is visible to other users)
  --connect-timeout <dur>  give up reaching the desk after <dur> (default 60s; 30s, 3m)
```

```text
through the hosted API:
  --via api                through the GaiaDesk API instead of peer to peer (end-to-end encrypted
                           when the desk publishes its key); `--via direct` is the default
```

exit codes: 0 done; 1 it ran and did not succeed (a file failed, no such job);
254 the desk refused (credential, a token without the scope, permission); 255 this CLI's own error.
The session is the held one `exec` and `shell` use (per desk and credential; $GAIADESK_PERSIST).

> **JSON:** with `--json` this command prints one JSON document on stdout (or the error envelope `{"error":{"kind","message"}}` on failure). The exact shape is defined in the JSON Schema printed by `gaiadesk-cli schema --json`; see also [JSON output](#json-output).

## ps

List a desk's background jobs.

**Usage**

```text
gaiadesk-cli ps --desk-id <id> [--mine] [--json]
```

Each job's name, state (queued, running, exited, killed, lost — and why a desk stopped it, e.g.
`killed (memory limit 512 MB)`), exit code, pid, log size, its caps (priority, cpu, mem,
keep-awake) and command. `lost` means the job's process is gone and how it ended was never
recorded (the machine restarted, or its wrapper was killed from outside): its exit code is
unknown. A GaiaDesk restart alone never loses a job — the next host adopts it (by pid and that
process's start time, so a reused pid is not mistaken for it) and records its real exit code.
A job that exited 127 within seconds is noted `command not found: <program>`. `--json` prints {"jobs":[…]} and adds
`limits` and `enforcement`: how this desk enforces each cap, and what it could not. Every job
carries `max_running`, the desk's limit on jobs running at once; a `queued` job has its
`queue_position`. A token needs the `jobs` scope. --mine: only the jobs this credential started
(this agent token's; with the desk's code, the owner's own).

output:
  -q, --quiet              no progress or notes on stderr (the result and errors still print)
```

                           $GAIADESK_CODE or the prompt: argv is visible to other users)

```

254 the desk refused (credential, a token without the scope, permission); 255 this CLI's own error.

## wait

Block until a background job ends.

**Usage**

```text
gaiadesk-cli wait <job> --desk-id <id> [--timeout <dur>] [--json]
```

Returns when the job is no longer running, and exits with ITS exit code (a job that was killed
or lost, with no code: 1). The desk holds the request until then (an older desk is asked every
second instead). If the link to the desk drops, `wait` redials by itself (for up to 5 minutes, and
within --timeout) and carries on: the job belongs to the desk, so nothing is lost. A queued job
is waited for through its queue time. A token needs the `jobs` scope.

**Options**

| Flag | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--timeout <dur>` | give up after &lt;dur&gt; (30s, 10m, 2h): exit 124, the job still running |
| `--json` | one object: the job's fields (`state`, `exit_code`, `reason`, …) plus `outcome` (finished \| timed_out \| link_lost \| desk_slept \| desk_offline) and `exit_status`, the code this command exits with. When the link is lost: state "link_lost", exit_code null, reason desk_slept \| desk_offline \| connection_lost. |

When the link is gone for good, `wait` asks the GaiaDesk server (no dial) where the desk is: asleep
(`gaiadesk-cli wake` it, then `wait` again — start long jobs with `run --keep-awake`), offline,
or online/unknown.

exit codes: the job's own exit code (0 = success); 1 no such job, or it ended without a code
(killed, lost); 75 the link was lost and could not be regained — the job may still be running,
`wait` again; 76 the link was lost and the desk is ASLEEP (desk_slept); 77 the link was lost and
the desk is OFFLINE (desk_offline); 124 --timeout ran out, the job still running; 254 the desk
refused; 255 this CLI's own error (offline, unreachable, bad arguments). A job can itself exit
75, 76, 77 or 124: read `outcome`.

```text
output:
  -q, --quiet              no progress or notes on stderr (the result and errors still print)
```

```text
credentials (see `gaiadesk-cli --help` for the order):
  --token-file <file>      a scoped agent token (or $GAIADESK_TOKEN_FILE)
  --code <code>            the desk's code — refused unless --allow-code-in-argv too (prefer
                           $GAIADESK_CODE or the prompt: argv is visible to other users)
```

```text
through the hosted API:
  --via api                through the GaiaDesk API instead of peer to peer (end-to-end encrypted
                           when the desk publishes its key); `--via direct` is the default
```

## kill

Stop a background job and everything it started.

**Usage**

```text
gaiadesk-cli kill <job> --desk-id <id> [--force] [--json]
```

Stops the job politely, then by force after 3 seconds, along with every process it started
(its process group on macOS/Linux, its Job object on Windows). A queued job is taken out of the
line. A job that runs past `run --max-runtime` is stopped the same way.
An agent token stops only the jobs IT started (refused, 254, otherwise; nor may it start a job
under another caller's job name); the desk's owner (its code or password) stops any.
--force: another caller's job, for a token with the `admin` scope.

## health

A desk's figures, and when to be warned.

**Usage**

```text
gaiadesk-cli health <desk> [--json]
gaiadesk-cli health set <desk> [--disk-free <pct>] [--swap <pct>] [--load <n>] [--json]
```

**Subcommands:** `set`

`health <desk>` asks the desk for its `stats` and holds them against the thresholds — the ones
`health set` keeps on the server when this machine is signed in, else the defaults below — one
line per check, `ok` or `WARN`: each volume's free space (also WARN under 5 GB free), swap,
5-minute load per CPU, memory pressure (macOS). --json: the `stats --json` object plus
checks:[{kind, ok, text}], healthy, thresholds:{limits, source: server|default}.
Exit codes: 0 every check ok; 1 a threshold is crossed; 254 refused; 255 unreachable or this
CLI's own error.
Every online desk reports its free disk (the fullest volume), swap and load to the GaiaDesk
server every 5 minutes. The server compares them with the desk's thresholds and, when one is
crossed, shows a warning on the desk in the devices list and sends the `desk.health` webhook —
once per condition per 6 hours. Defaults: disk free under 10%, swap over 75% used, 5-minute load
over 2 per CPU (macOS: memory pressure critical always counts).
`health set` changes them (a number, `off`, or `default`); with no flags it prints them and the
desk's warnings at its last report. Signs in as an ACCOUNT, like `wake`: $GAIADESK_API_KEY,
`gaiadesk-cli login`, $GAIADESK_TOKEN or the app's sign-in on this machine. The account page's
devices list shows the same warnings.

## disk

Where a desk's space went.

**Usage**

```text
gaiadesk-cli disk <desk> [<path>] [--top N] [--budget <dur>] [--json]
```

The largest entries of &lt;path&gt; on the desk (default: the desk user's home; relative paths are from
it), each folder with everything under it, biggest first. The desk walks the folder itself, on up
to 8 threads, for at most --budget (default 20s, at most 2m) — and when the budget runs out first
it says PARTIAL and shows what it counted, never a silent timeout (`exec du` can run for many
minutes on a full build disk). Symlinks are not followed; another volume (a mount point, a Windows
junction) is named and not entered; folders it may not read are counted as such. Sizes are what
the files take on disk. Needs the desk's file access (a token: the `cp` scope; a confined token:
a path inside its directory).
Then the Clearable caches that exist for the desk's user, each with its size (a short walk each,
a quarter of --budget between them): macOS ~/Library/Caches (and Homebrew's in it),
~/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData; Windows %TEMP%, %LOCALAPPDATA%\npm-cache and pip\Cache;
Linux ~/.cache; everywhere ~/.npm/_cacache and ~/.cargo/registry/cache. Listed only — `disk`
never deletes anything.

**Options**

| Flag | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--top <n>` | how many entries (default 15, at most 200) |
| `--budget <dur>` | how long the desk may walk: 5s, 1m (default 20s) |
| `--json` | {root, entries:[{name, dir, bytes, files}], total_bytes, files, partial, other_volumes, unreadable, elapsed_ms, caches:[{name, path, bytes, partial}]} |

```text
output:
  -q, --quiet              no progress or notes on stderr (the result and errors still print)
```

```text
credentials (see `gaiadesk-cli --help` for the order):
  --token-file <file>      a scoped agent token (or $GAIADESK_TOKEN_FILE)
  --code <code>            the desk's code — refused unless --allow-code-in-argv too (prefer
                           $GAIADESK_CODE or the prompt: argv is visible to other users)
  --connect-timeout <dur>  give up reaching the desk after <dur> (default 60s; 30s, 3m)
```

## token

Scoped, expiring agent tokens, administered by the desk's owner.

**Usage**

```text
gaiadesk-cli token create --desk <id>[,<id>…] [--name <n>] [--expires 7d] [--scope exec,cp,jobs]
                          [--cwd <dir on the desk>] [--low-priv] [--out <file>] [--json]
gaiadesk-cli token list --desk <id> [--json]         ({"tokens":[…]})
gaiadesk-cli token revoke --desk <id> (<name|id> | --all-for-desk) [--account]
```

**Subcommands:** `create`, `list`, `revoke`

The credential to give an AI agent instead of the desk's password. Owner only: these present the
desk's unattended password (never a token). Defaults: 7 days, scopes exec,cp,jobs.
Scopes: exec (one command), shell (an interactive shell), cp, forward, jobs (= run), screen —
and admin, never implied: exec/shell/cp may ask for --admin, which the desk's owner must also
allow at the desk (Settings → Agent access → Admin access).
--cwd: the token's commands, shells and jobs start there and every path it copies must be inside
it (links resolved). --low-priv: they run as the desk's low-privilege agent user (Settings →
Agent access on the desk), or are refused. The desk enforces both. Several desks: one token each,
all in one --out file. `--out` writes a private (0600) file for --token-file; otherwise each token
is printed once. A revoke takes effect at once: its sessions are dropped and its jobs stopped;
--account revokes through the GaiaDesk server as the account signed in here (no password).

```text
through the hosted API:
  --via api                through the GaiaDesk API instead of peer to peer (end-to-end encrypted
                           when the desk publishes its key); `--via direct` is the default
```

exit codes: 0 done; 1 it ran and did not succeed (a file failed, no such job);
254 the desk refused (credential, a token without the scope, permission); 255 this CLI's own error.
The session is the held one `exec` and `shell` use (per desk and credential; $GAIADESK_PERSIST).

## connect

Open (or reuse) a held connection to a desk.

**Usage**

```text
gaiadesk-cli connect --desk-id <id> [--wait <secs>] [options]
```

Opens a connection to the desk and holds it for later commands (the same held session
`exec`, `shell`, `cp` and the other desk commands use). Exits 0 when the desk is
reachable.

With --wait &lt;secs&gt;: blocks until the desk is reachable (up to &lt;secs&gt; seconds), retrying
every 5 seconds. Useful in CI or scripts that start a machine and need to wait for
GaiaDesk to come online before running commands:

gaiadesk-cli connect --desk-id 123456789 --wait 120
gaiadesk-cli exec --desk-id 123456789 -- hostname

Without --wait: dials once; exits 1 if the desk is not reachable.

**Options**

| Flag | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--desk-id <id>` | the desk (-d) |
| `--wait <secs>` | block up to this many seconds for the desk to become reachable; exit 1 on timeout (minimum 1) |
| `--connect-timeout <dur>` | give up on each dial attempt after &lt;dur&gt; (default 60s) |
| `--persist <dur>` | keep the connection open for this long idle (default 10m) |
| `-q, --quiet` | no progress lines on stderr |
| `--json` | exit-status JSON: {"desk_id","ok":true} or the error envelope |

exit codes: 0 reachable · 1 not reachable within --wait · 254 refused · 255 this CLI's error.

```text
credentials (see `gaiadesk-cli --help` for the order):
  --token-file <file>      a scoped agent token (or $GAIADESK_TOKEN_FILE)
  --code <code>            the desk's code — refused unless --allow-code-in-argv too (prefer
                           $GAIADESK_CODE or the prompt: argv is visible to other users)
```

## doctor

Check that a desk is fully operational.

**Usage**

```text
gaiadesk-cli doctor --desk-id <id> [options]
```

Runs a checklist against the desk and prints the result:

[ok] credential: agent token for desk 123456789
[ok] connect: via mesh (45ms)
[ok] exec: echo round-trip 230ms
[ok] cp-up: 512 bytes in 120ms
[ok] cp-down: 512 bytes in 95ms, verified
[ok] all checks passed

Each check is independent: a connect failure skips exec, cp-up and cp-down (there is
nothing to run them on), but all checks that can be run are run. Exits 0 when all pass,
1 when any fail.

| `--desk-id <id>` | the desk (-d) |
| `--connect-timeout <dur>` | give up reaching the desk after &lt;dur&gt; (default 60s) |
| `--json` | one JSON object: {"desk_id", "checks": [{"name", "ok", "detail"}], "all_ok": true\|false} |

exit codes: 0 all checks passed · 1 one or more checks failed · 254 refused · 255 this CLI's error.

## watch

Stream presence events for a desk.

**Usage**

```text
gaiadesk-cli watch --desk-id <id> [--interval <secs>] [--json]
```

Polls the GaiaDesk server for the desk's online/offline state and emits an event each time it
changes. Runs until Ctrl+C. Useful for monitoring and automation — pipe it to a script that
reacts to desk state changes.

The first event is emitted on the first poll (the initial state). Subsequent events are emitted
only when the state changes (online → offline or offline → online). No output when the state is
unchanged between polls. One line per event, always to stdout.

The desk must be on your account or team. Requires this machine to be signed in to GaiaDesk.

**Options**

| Flag | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--desk-id <id>` | the desk to watch (-d) |
| `--interval <n>` | how often to poll the server, in seconds (default: 10; minimum: 1) |
| `--json` | one JSON object per line: online:  {"event":"online",  "desk_id":"123456789", "time":"2026-10-12T14:30:00Z"} offline: {"event":"offline", "desk_id":"123456789", "time":"2026-10-12T14:35:00Z"} |

```text
Without --json:
  [14:30] desk 123456789 online
  [14:35] desk 123456789 offline
```

**Examples**

```sh
gaiadesk-cli watch -d 123456789
gaiadesk-cli watch -d 123456789 --json
gaiadesk-cli watch -d 123456789 --interval 30 --json | jq .
```

exit codes: 0 Ctrl+C · 1 not signed in · 255 error

> **JSON:** with `--json` this command prints one JSON document on stdout (or the error envelope `{"error":{"kind","message"}}` on failure). The exact shape is defined in the JSON Schema printed by `gaiadesk-cli schema --json`; see also [JSON output](#json-output).

## changelog

User-visible changes to this CLI and agent.

**Usage**

```text
gaiadesk-cli changelog [--since <version>] [--json]
```

A built-in list of changes that affect how an AI agent or script uses `gaiadesk-cli`: new flags,
changed defaults, bug fixes in exec/cp/shell/auth, and protocol changes that affect available
commands or their behaviour. UI-only changes are not listed.

The list is ordered newest first. Without --since, all known entries are printed.

```text
--since <version>   only print entries at or after this version (e.g. 0.10.300)
--json              one JSON array:
                      [{"version":"0.10.335","change":"exec: --kill-tree-on-disconnect …"}, …]
```

**Examples**

```sh
gaiadesk-cli changelog
gaiadesk-cli changelog --since 0.10.300
gaiadesk-cli changelog --json | jq '.[] | select(.version >= "0.10.320")'
```

exit codes: 0 always

$GAIADESK_AGENT_TOKEN and is never printed. --json: {"desk_id","ok":true,"screenshot":{"width","height"}},
or the error envelope.

> **JSON:** with `--json` this command prints one JSON document on stdout (or the error envelope `{"error":{"kind","message"}}` on failure). The exact shape is defined in the JSON Schema printed by `gaiadesk-cli schema --json`; see also [JSON output](#json-output).

## init-agent

Create a scoped agent token and save it, ready to use.

**Usage**

```text
gaiadesk-cli init-agent --desk-id <id> [--scopes exec,cp,jobs] [--ttl 7d] [--name <n>] [--json]
```

The fast path for setting up an AI agent: mints a scoped token, writes it to
~/.gaiadesk/tokens/&lt;desk-id&gt;-agent.json (owner-only, 0600), and prints the
export line on stdout:

export GAIADESK_TOKEN_FILE=/Users/you/.gaiadesk/tokens/123456789-agent.json

Copy-paste it, or eval the whole command:

eval $(gaiadesk-cli init-agent --desk-id 123456789)

The agent then presents the token with --token-file or $GAIADESK_TOKEN_FILE.
--json: {"tokens":[…], "file":"&lt;path&gt;"} — the file path and what each token allows.
Defaults: scopes exec,cp,jobs (one command, file copy, background jobs), TTL 7 days.
Owner only: requires the desk's unattended password (prompted on a terminal, or
$GAIADESK_CODE). An existing agent token is never accepted here.

```text
credentials (see `gaiadesk-cli --help` for the order):
  --token-file <file>      a scoped agent token (or $GAIADESK_TOKEN_FILE)
  --code <code>            the desk's code — refused unless --allow-code-in-argv too (prefer
                           $GAIADESK_CODE or the prompt: argv is visible to other users)
```

> **JSON:** with `--json` this command prints one JSON document on stdout (or the error envelope `{"error":{"kind","message"}}` on failure). The exact shape is defined in the JSON Schema printed by `gaiadesk-cli schema --json`; see also [JSON output](#json-output).

## agent run

Drive a desk with a model (Agent Access).

**Usage**

```text
gaiadesk-cli agent run --desk-id <id> (--task <text> | --task-file <path>) [options]
```

```text
options: --model <m> --max-steps <n> --max-duration <secs> --long-edge <px> --token-budget <n>
         --max-tokens <n> --allow-domain <d> --server <wss://…/ws> --token <t> --name <n>
         --out-dir <dir> --keep-runs <n> --report <path> --junit <path>
The model key comes from $ANTHROPIC_API_KEY; the agent token from --token or $GAIADESK_AGENT_TOKEN.
Exit: 0 passed, 1 failed, 2 no verdict, 3 stopped by a human, 4 refused; 254/255 as elsewhere.
```

## mcp

GaiaDesk tools over the Model Context Protocol.

**Usage**

```text
gaiadesk-cli mcp [--stdio | --http [--bind <ip>] [--port <n>] [--allow-origin <o>]]
                 [--server <wss://…/ws>] [--allow-domain <d>] [--audit-dir <dir>]
```

stdio by default (--stdio says so explicitly). Screen tools need an agent token in $GAIADESK_AGENT_TOKEN. The desk tools —
gaiadesk_exec (one command, exit code and separate streams; `env`, `shell`), gaiadesk_copy_files,
gaiadesk_job_run (`env`, `shell`), gaiadesk_job_list, gaiadesk_job_logs, gaiadesk_job_wait,
gaiadesk_job_kill, gaiadesk_forward_\* — ride the held connections the CLI uses and present, over stdio, an agent token
from $GAIADESK_TOKEN_FILE, else $GAIADESK_CODE, else the agent token; over HTTP, only the agent token.
The desk tools return `structuredContent` and list an `outputSchema`. Every tool is listed below.

Protocol: the standard lifecycle (initialize → notifications/initialized → requests, ping) at
2025-11-25, 2025-06-18, 2025-03-26 and 2024-11-05 — over HTTP with an Mcp-Session-Id — and the
stateless 2026-07-28 revision (per-request _meta, server/discover, mirrored headers).

Tool names are [a-zA-Z0-9_-] (gaiadesk_exec, gaiadesk_screenshot, …).

```text
--audit-dir <dir>  where each session's record goes (default: mcp-audit in this user's GaiaDesk
                   data directory — never the directory the client started the server in).
```

```text
tools (screen tools need $GAIADESK_AGENT_TOKEN; the rest are the desk tools):
  gaiadesk_open_session        Open a desk session
  gaiadesk_close_session       Close a desk session
  gaiadesk_screenshot          See the screen
  gaiadesk_click               Click
  gaiadesk_move_pointer        Move the pointer
  gaiadesk_drag                Drag
  gaiadesk_press_button        Hold or release the left button
  gaiadesk_scroll              Scroll
  gaiadesk_type_text           Type text
  gaiadesk_press_keys          Press a key combination
  gaiadesk_hold_keys           Hold a key combination
  gaiadesk_wait                Wait
  gaiadesk_pointer_position    Where is the pointer
  gaiadesk_exec                Run a command on a desk
  gaiadesk_copy_files          Copy files to or from a desk
  gaiadesk_job_run             Start a background job on a desk
  gaiadesk_job_list            List a desk's background jobs
  gaiadesk_job_logs            Read a background job's output
  gaiadesk_job_wait            Wait for a background job to end
  gaiadesk_job_kill            Stop a background job
  gaiadesk_forward_start       Forward a local port to a desk
  gaiadesk_forward_stop        Stop a port forward
  gaiadesk_desk_status         Check a desk's reachability and load
  gaiadesk_jobs_wait           Wait for several background jobs to end
  gaiadesk_desk_stats          Read a desk's CPU, memory and disks
  gaiadesk_desk_wake           Wake a sleeping desk
  gaiadesk_git_sync            Put a git commit on a desk
  gaiadesk_pull_changed        Copy a desk checkout's changes here
```

## schema

The JSON Schema of every --json shape.

**Usage**

```text
gaiadesk-cli schema [--json]
```

One JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) with every result, error, request and event type of
gaiadesk-client — and so of every `--json` output — under $defs (`x-roots` names the ones a call
returns or takes). scripts/gen-sdk-types.mts turns it into TypeScript and Python types.

> **JSON:** with `--json` this command prints one JSON document on stdout (or the error envelope `{"error":{"kind","message"}}` on failure). The exact shape is defined in the JSON Schema printed by `gaiadesk-cli schema --json`; see also [JSON output](#json-output).

## api

Call the hosted GaiaDesk API, like `gh api`.

**Usage**

```text
gaiadesk-cli api <METHOD> <path> [--data <json> | --data @<file> | --data @-]
                 [-H "Name: value"]... [--api-key <key>] [--json]
```

&lt;path&gt; is under /v1 (`/desks`, `desks/123456789/stats`, `/v1/audit?limit=5`). The answer goes to
stdout: JSON pretty-printed (one line with --json), an event stream or a file's bytes as they
come. A failure is the API's error envelope on stdout, its message on stderr.

Calls as you: this CLI's own sign-in (`gaiadesk-cli login`; the app's sign-in is this computer's
own, which the API does not take), or an API key: --api-key &lt;key&gt; or $GAIADESK_API_KEY.
$GAIADESK_API_URL points it elsewhere (default: the server's /v1). A desk's agent token goes in
a header: -H "X-GaiaDesk-Desk-Token: gdagt_…".
--data sends JSON (or, when it is not JSON, the bytes as they are). A raw call is sent as
written: it is not end-to-end encrypted (`--via api` on exec, cp, run… is).

**Examples**

```sh
gaiadesk-cli api GET /desks
gaiadesk-cli api POST /desks/123456789/exec --data '{"command": "uname -a"}'
```

exit codes: 0 a 2xx answer · 1 failed · 254 refused · 255 this CLI's error (usage, unreachable)

> **JSON:** with `--json` this command prints one JSON document on stdout (or the error envelope `{"error":{"kind","message"}}` on failure). The exact shape is defined in the JSON Schema printed by `gaiadesk-cli schema --json`; see also [JSON output](#json-output).

## login, logout

Sign this CLI in (shows a code to approve in a browser)

**Usage**

```text
gaiadesk-cli login [--json]    sign this CLI in (shows a code to approve in a browser)
gaiadesk-cli logout [--json]   sign this CLI out (ends its Atlas session and sign-in)
```

The server is $GAIADESK_SERVER (a wss:// URL), else production.

```text
--json: one JSON object per line on stdout. login: first
  {"event":"code","verification_uri":…,"verification_uri_complete":…,"user_code":…}
(show it to the person who approves), then {"event":"signed_in","email":…} — or the error
envelope {"error":{"kind","message"}}. logout: {"event":"signed_out"}.
```

> **JSON:** with `--json` this command prints one JSON document on stdout (or the error envelope `{"error":{"kind","message"}}` on failure). The exact shape is defined in the JSON Schema printed by `gaiadesk-cli schema --json`; see also [JSON output](#json-output).

## JSON output

The shapes a program can rely on.

```text
ERRORS: every command that takes --json prints, on stdout, when it fails:
  {"error": {"kind": "<kind>", "message": "<a sentence>", "reason": "<finer cause, sometimes>"}}
kind is one of six:
  usage            bad arguments — fix the call                          (exit 255)
  refused          the desk or server said no: credential, scope, permission, a confined
                   token's directory                                       (exit 254)
  unreachable      the desk or server could not be reached: offline, unknown id, no route,
                   timed out (`reason`: offline, unknown_desk, not_online, network,
                   not_signed_in, timeout)                                (exit 255)
  connection_lost  reached, and the connection went away mid-request      (exit 255; shell 253)
  failed           allowed, and it did not succeed: no such job, a file failed, a local error
                                                                         (exit 1, or 255)
  protocol         the desk answered something this CLI cannot use — usually a GaiaDesk too
                   old for the request (update it)                         (exit 255)
Refused-vs-failed comes from the desk itself (a field on its answer), not from its words.
exec/shell --json keep their whole object and put the same {kind, message, reason} in `error`.
The human sentence still goes to stderr.

SHAPES: ps {"jobs":[…]} · token list {"tokens":[…]} · audit {"events":[…]} · devices {"devices":[…]}
  · logs {"job","output"} (-f: events) · mesh ip {"desk_id","mesh_ip","renamed_to"}
  · wait: the job {"name","state","exit_code",…} · whoami {"source","account"}
  · devices also {"identity":{"source","account"}} · disconnect {"closed":[…]} · agent-connect {"desk_id","ok","screenshot"}
  · login/logout: events {"event":"code"|"signed_in"|"signed_out"}
  · exec --json-stream: {"event":"stdout"|"stderr","data"} … {"event":"exit"|"error"}
  · --version --json {"name","version","features":[…],"mcp_protocol_versions"}
```

The JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) of every result, error, request and event type is printed by `gaiadesk-cli schema --json`; the SDKs generate their types from it.
